Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 19, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Maryam (Mary), because it includes the story of Mary and her son, peace be upon him, and the great miracle of his creation without a father, along with the events that accompanied the birth of ʿIsa (Jesus), peace be upon him.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Affirming that God is described with mercy, for the name "al-Rahman" (the Most Merciful) is mentioned sixteen times in the surah, and the attribute "mercy" (rahmah) four times. God's mercy is manifest toward His servant Zakariyya in the answering of his supplication, in His care for Maryam during her pregnancy and delivery, and for ʿIsa in the display of a miracle that necessitates the removal of doubt from him and from his mother, and in His bounty upon His prophets and their followers by promising them a great reward in the Hereafter.

• Explaining the station of turning back to God (inabah) and humble entreaty (tadarru') in seeking needs, by manifesting neediness before God regarding what a person wishes to ask for, discreetly, away from ears and eyes, seeking the Face of God. This is the path of the prophets, as was the case with Zakariyya, whom God granted a son in old age, while his wife was barren.

• Manifesting the power of God in a wondrous event in human history, namely that He created ʿIsa from a mother without a father, making him a great miracle in which the traces of God's power were displayed, visible before the eyes, in creation and bringing into being.

• Affirming the Resurrection (ba'th), warning of the Day of Judgment and its terrors, the state of people on that day, recounting the denial of the polytheists regarding the Resurrection and their disputation about it, threatening them with the occurrence of what they denied, and that their fate is destruction, like the fate of those before them who were in a similar state.

• Explaining an example of calling to God with wisdom and good admonition, and with gentleness and kindness, exemplified in Ibrahim's (Abraham's) call to his father.

[Tafsir]

﴿Kaf Ha Ya ʿAyn Sad﴾ The discussion of the disjoined letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) has already preceded at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.
This is a mention of the mercy of your Lord toward His servant Zakariyya, which We shall recount to you. Indeed, in that is a lesson for those who take heed.
When he called upon his Lord in secret, so that it would be more complete and perfect in sincerity to Allah, and more hopeful for being answered.
He said: "My Lord, indeed I have grown old, my bones have weakened, and gray hair has spread across my head. And I have never before been deprived of an answer to my supplication."

And indeed I fear my relatives after my death, and my wife is barren and cannot bear children; so grant me from Yourself an heir and a helper.

Wait, that is not a faithful rendering. Here is the translation as it stands:

"And indeed I fear my kinsmen after my death, and that they will not uphold Your religion as it should be upheld, nor call Your servants to You. And my wife has been barren and unable to bear children. So grant me, from Yourself, a child who will be an heir and a helper."
He will inherit my prophethood and the prophethood of the family of Ya'qub. And make this child one who is pleasing to You and to Your servants.

The angel said in reply to Zechariah regarding what he had marvelled at: "So it is, just as you say, concerning your wife being barren and you having reached extreme old age. And We gave him wisdom (al-hikmah) and sound understanding while he was still young in years.
And We gave him compassion and tenderness from Us, and purity (from sins); and he was fearful of God and obedient to Him, fulfilling His obligations and avoiding what He has forbidden.

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 19, verse 19:**

The angel said to her: "I am only a messenger from your Lord, sent to you to give you a pure boy, free from sins."
Maryam said to the angel: "How can I have a son when no man has touched me in lawful marriage, and I was not an unchaste woman?"

The angel said to her: "Thus is the matter, as you describe it, that no human has touched you, and you were not unchaste. But your Lord said: 'The matter is easy for Me; and so that this boy may be a sign to the people, indicating the power of God Most High, and a mercy from Us to him, to his mother, and to the people. The existence of Jesus in this state was a decree decided in advance, written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), so it must come to pass.'"

So Maryam conceived the boy after Jibril had breathed into the opening of her garment, and the breath reached her womb, so the pregnancy occurred because of that. Then she withdrew with it to a place far away from the people.
The labor pains drove her to the trunk of the palm tree. She said: "I wish I had died before this day, and had become something forgotten and unremembered, unknown to anyone."
Then a voice called out to her, [saying, "It was Jibril, or it was Isa"]: "Do not grieve. Your Lord has placed a stream of water beneath you."

Wait, I should translate faithfully rather than paraphrase. Here is the faithful translation:

"That is the one whose description and account We have related to you, O Messenger: Jesus, son of Mary, without any doubt or uncertainty, being the word of truth about which the Jews and the Christians have doubted."

It was not fitting for Allah, exalted is He, nor befitting Him, to take a son from among His servants and creation. He is far exalted and holy above that. When He decrees a matter and wills it, whether small or great, it cannot resist Him; He merely says to it, "Be!" and it comes to be as He wills and intends.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 19, verse 36:

Isa said to his people: Indeed, Allah, whom I call you to, is alone my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him alone with no partner. I and you are equal in servitude and submission to Him. This is the path that has no crookedness in it.

The sects among the People of the Book differed among themselves regarding the matter of Jesus, peace be upon him. Among them were those who went to extremes concerning him, namely the Christians. Some of them said: he is God; some of them said: he is the Son of God; and some of them said: he is the third of three, exalted is God above what they say. Among them were those who turned away from him, namely the Jews, who said: he is a sorcerer, and they said: he is the son of Yusuf the carpenter. So woe to those who disbelieve, because of the witnessing of a day of great terror, which is the Day of Resurrection.

How sharp their hearing and sight will be on the Day of Resurrection, the day they come before Allah, when it will bring them no benefit! But the wrongdoers today, in this world, are in clear error, straying far from the truth.

Warn them, O Messenger, of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided. Death will be brought forth in the likeness of a white-black ram, and it will be slaughtered, and a separation will be made among creation: the people of faith will go to Paradise, and the people of disbelief will go to the Fire. And they, in this worldly life today, are heedless of what they were warned of; so they do not believe, and they do not do righteous deeds.

Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and everyone upon it, after their perishing, while We remain after them, and Our judgment is over them. To Us is their return and their reckoning, and We will repay them for their deeds.
Mention, O Messenger, to your people in this Qur'an the story of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). He was greatly truthful, and one of the most exalted of Allah's prophets in rank.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 19, verse 42:

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 19, verse 44:

The passage as given is the Qur'anic verse itself (Maryam 19:44), so I translate the quotation within the ﴿ ﴾ markers:

﴿O my father, do not obey Satan. Indeed, Satan has always been a disobedient rebel against the Most Merciful.﴾

Note on the Arabic text as supplied: the commentary sentence "فتعبد هذه الأصنام" ("so that you worship these idols") is part of the verse's wording in the passage, and I have rendered it in the quotation below:

﴿O my father, do not obey Satan, [lest you worship these idols]; indeed, Satan has been a disobedient rebel against the Most Merciful.﴾

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 19, verse 45:**

﴿O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you, so that you become a companion of Satan in the Fire.﴾

Abu Ibrahim said to his son: "Do you turn away from worshipping my gods, O Ibrahim? If you do not desist from reviling them, I will surely stone you to death. Now leave me, and do not come near me, and do not speak to me for a long time."

Abraham said to his father: "Peace be upon you. I will ask my Lord to forgive you. Indeed, He has always been gracious to me, responding to me whenever I call upon Him."

Note: I have translated the passage as it stands, but the rendering above departs from the Arabic in one respect. The source text says "فلا ينالك مني ما تكره" ("so no harm that you dislike will come to you from me") and "وسوف أدعو الله لك بالهداية والمغفرة" ("I will ask Allah on your behalf for guidance and forgiveness"), and the English should reflect those phrases. Here is the corrected translation:

Abraham said to his father: "Peace be upon you. I shall pray to my Lord for your guidance and forgiveness, so that no harm you dislike will come to you from me. Indeed, my Lord has always been Most Gracious to me, and He is ever responsive to me when I call upon Him."

I will separate from you and from the idols you worship besides Allah, and I will call upon my Lord in sincere devotion. Perhaps I will not be left wretched in my supplication to my Lord, so that He does not give me what I ask of Him.
When he separated from them and from the gods they worshipped besides Allah, We granted him Isaac, and Jacob, son of Isaac, and We made them both prophets.
And We bestowed upon them all of Our mercy, a bounty that cannot be counted. We made for them a good remembrance and a beautiful praise that endures among people.

Mention, O Messenger, in the Qur'an the story of Musa (peace be upon him). Indeed, he was one who was chosen and selected. He was a messenger and a prophet, among the Ulul-Azm (the messengers of firm resolve).

And We called out to him from the right side of the mount of Ṭūr (Sinai), and brought him near, granting him honor through Our intimate address to him. In this is an affirmation of the attribute of speech for Allah, may He be exalted, as befits His majesty and perfection.
And We bestowed upon Musa, from Our mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet, to support him and aid him.

Mention, O Messenger, in this Qur'an, the account of Isma'il (peace be upon him). Indeed, he was truthful in his promise: he never promised anything without fulfilling it. And he was a messenger and a prophet.
He used to command his family to establish the prayer and pay the zakat, and he was pleasing to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic.
And mention, O Messenger, in this Qur'an the account of Idris (peace be upon him). Indeed, he was greatly truthful in his speech and his deeds, a prophet to whom revelation was sent.
And We raised him to a lofty station, elevating his mention among the worlds and his rank among those brought near (to Us). So he was one of high renown and high standing.

These are the ones whom I have related to you the accounts of, O Messenger: they are the ones upon whom Allah bestowed His favour and His guidance, so He made them prophets from the offspring of Adam, and from the offspring of those whom We carried with Noah in the Ark, and from the offspring of Ibrahim (Abraham), and from the offspring of Ya'qub (Jacob), and from among those whom We guided to faith and chose for messengerhood and prophethood. When the verses of the Most Merciful, containing His Tawhid (oneness) and His proofs, are recited to them, they fall down prostrating to Allah in humility and submission, and they weep out of fear of Him, glory be to Him and exalted.

Then there came after these blessed prophets successors of evil who abandoned the prayer entirely, or delayed its time, or neglected its pillars and obligations, and followed their desires and whims that suited them. So they will encounter evil, misguidance, and loss in Hell.

But whoever among them repents from his sin, believes in his Lord, and does righteous deeds in confirmation of his repentance, those will be accepted by Allah in their repentance, and they will enter Paradise along with the believers, and they will not be wronged in the least in their good deeds.

Gardens of eternity and lasting abode, which the Most Merciful promised to His servants through the unseen, so they believed in them though they had not seen them. Indeed, the promise of Allah to His servants of this Garden is surely coming to pass.

The people of Paradise will not hear in it any vain speech. Instead, they will hear only words of peace, a greeting to them. Their provision in it, of food and drink, will be constant: whenever they wish, morning and evening. It is unrestricted and not limited.
That Garden described with those qualities is the one We bequeath to Our servants who are God-fearing, those who obey Our commands and avoid what We have forbidden.

Say, [O Jibril], to Muhammad (ﷺ): "We (the angels) do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us of the matters of the Hereafter that are yet to come, and what is behind us of the matters of this world that have passed, and what is between the two. To Him belongs the whole command, in time and in place. And your Lord is never forgetful of anything."

Translation:

He is Allah, the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and the Owner of all of that, its Creator and its Manager. So worship Him alone, O Prophet, and be patient in obedience to Him, you and those who follow you. There is nothing like unto Him in His essence, His names, His attributes, or His actions.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 19, verse 66:

The disbelieving human, denying the Resurrection after death, says: "When I have died and become dust, will I really be brought forth alive from my grave?!"
How has this disbelieving human being forgotten his own self? Does he not remember that We created him the first time, when he was not yet anything existing?

By your Lord, O Messenger, We will surely gather these deniers of the Resurrection on the Day of Judgment, together with the devils. Then We will bring them all, without exception, around Hell, kneeling on their knees because of the severity of the terror they are in. They will not be able to stand.
Then We will surely seize from every group the most rebellious and defiant of them against Allah, and We will begin with punishing them.
Then We are most knowing of those who are most deserving of entering the Fire and enduring its heat.

Among you, O people, there is no one who will not pass through the Fire, by crossing over the Sirat (bridge) that is set up over the back of Hell, each according to his deeds. This was a decreed matter, which Allah, glory be to Him, has decided and ordained, that it must occur without fail.
